tweet_summary: A video filmed from a car in Dubai during the March 2026 Iran war, with a voiceover and overlay claiming that the missiles hitting Gulf nations are coming 'from the direction of Israel, not Iran' — i.e. an Israeli false-flag, because (the speaker argues) rockets seen flying over the Jebel Ali seaport could not have come from Iran's direction.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted. The tweet pushes a false-flag conspiracy: that Israel, not Iran, is behind the missile strikes on the UAE. Mainstream reporting and investigation (NYT, Bellingcat, Euronews, Time, UAE government) attribute the March 2026 strikes on Dubai/Abu Dhabi — including the Jebel Ali port fires — to Iran, launched in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The viral geographic 'proof' (missiles seen over the port must come from the west/Israel) is a single bystander's speculation; a top reply even notes the speaker has the geography wrong (anything launched from Iran to Dubai is seen over land). This is a checkable, high-reach misleading claim a reader benefits from correcting.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that the March 2026 missile/drone strikes on the UAE (including the Dubai / Jebel Ali port area shown) are attributed by credible reporting to IRAN — launched in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on Iran — and that there is NO credible evidence Israel launched missiles at the UAE; the 'missiles came from the direction of Israel' claim is an unsupported false-flag theory based on one bystander's flawed geographic reasoning. The note MUST cite genuinely loadable, on-point sources (e.g. NYT / Bellingcat / Reuters / Euronews / Time coverage of the Iranian strikes on the UAE). FAIL the original note's specific failure: do NOT cite a fabricated or dead UAE MoFA URL or sources that do not actually substantiate Iranian responsibility. Also FAIL any note that endorses or hedges toward the Israel false-flag claim, or that rests purely on the AI media description.
reference_note: Credible reporting attributes the March 2026 missile and drone strikes on the UAE — including the Jebel Ali/Dubai port fires shown — to Iran, launched in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on Iran. There is no evidence Israel fired missiles at the UAE. The claim that the rockets came 'from the direction of Israel' is an unverified false-flag theory; even the trajectory reasoning in the clip is disputed by other viewers. https://www.bellingcat.com/news/2026/04/02/war-uae-iran-infuencer-dubai-conflict-drone-successful-strike-intercept-fire/ https://www.euronews.com/2026/03/01/iranian-strikes-hit-dubai-and-abu-dhabi-damaging-airport-terminals-and-the-burj-al-arab

original_unhelpful_note.text: UAE Defence Ministry and joint statement with US and Gulf states confirm missile and drone attacks on Dubai originate from Iran in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes, with no evidence of Israeli launches toward UAE. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_United_Arab_Emirates https://www.mofa.gov.ae/en/MediaHub/News/2026/3/2/UAE-Iran-Attacks https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/4/hundreds-of-drones-target-kuwait-iraq-saudi-arabia-uae-amid-iran-war
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Rated notHelpfulSourcesMissingOrUnreliable (23). The note's verdict is correct, but it cites a likely-fabricated/dead UAE MoFA URL (mofa.gov.ae/.../UAE-Iran-Attacks) and an Al Jazeera link about drones targeting other countries that does not directly substantiate the Israel-vs-Iran attribution for Dubai. Raters also flagged it as argumentative/opinion. The note states a defensible conclusion but on sourcing that doesn't hold up.

fact_check.notes: Iran launched hundreds of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and ~1,835 drones at the UAE from late Feb-March 2026 in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on Iran; NYT and Bellingcat attribute the Jebel Ali port fires to an Iranian strike. No credible source supports an Israeli false-flag launch at the UAE. The clip's 'from the direction of Israel' claim is bystander speculation contradicted by reporting and by other viewers' geography corrections.

importance.lens_rationale: Wartime false-flag misinformation from a 214k-follower journalist with 480k+ impressions, in an active regional war; misattributing strikes to Israel could inflame escalation. Correcting conflict misattribution has clear global-stability relevance.
